definition: This means the IPU3 color correction matrix algorithm.
This refers to the frame buffer object to which a texture is attached.
It means the green R shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
It means the green B shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
The caller-specified category and severity level are used.

This is an interface that connects the graphics API with the display, image, and buffer of the operating environment. This document addresses the boundary for importing shared buffers as graphics images.
This is a kernel subsystem for managing Linux graphics devices. The DRM pixel format identifies channel layout within buffers.
This is a prefix used in identifiers for OpenGL family graphics APIs. The GL format in this document represents the channel configuration of textures.
A synchronization signal indicating when a buffer can be used. A request with a valid fence waits for the signal during preparation. This is different from request completion.
A request state that has not yet changed to complete or cancelled. It does not mean device processing has started; an earlier request in this state can delay later returns.
Information describing the controls and ranges available on a camera. The request control list must reference that camera’s information map.
A Stream associated with the current camera configuration. A request buffer referring to a stream from another configuration is rejected during submission checks.

A separate module (.so) holding the image-quality algorithms. It reads the statistics sent by the ISP and computes the ISP settings for the next frame. It is kept apart from libcamera itself so that vendors can ship it without publishing the source.
The processing unit that turns the sensor's raw (bayer) data into a usable image. It performs black-level correction, lens shading correction, white balance, debayering and more.
The libcamera component that does ISP processing on the CPU or GPU for devices without a hardware ISP. The source calls it software_isp and softisp.
Auto exposure (AE, AGC), auto white balance (AWB) and auto focus (AF) together. They are the main algorithms an IPA computes.
The auto-exposure algorithm that sets exposure time and sensor gain for the scene brightness.
The algorithm that estimates the colour temperature of the light and sets per-channel R, G and B gains so that white looks white.
The algorithm that moves the lens to bring the image into focus.
Correction for lens shading, where the image edges are darker or tinted compared with the centre because of the lens. It multiplies the image by a correction table laid out as a grid.
The baseline value a sensor outputs even with no light at all. It is subtracted in the first stage of ISP processing.
A colour filter array where each sensor pixel records only one of R, G or B. Raw data in this format needs debayering before every pixel has RGB values.
Interpolating each pixel's missing colours from its neighbours to turn bayer raw data into an RGB image. Also called demosaicing.
A small program that runs on the GPU. The software ISP can perform debayering and colour correction in GPU shaders.
A YAML file with per-sensor and per-platform algorithm parameters (correction tables, colour matrices and so on). The IPA reads it at start-up.
Precomputed results stored in a table and looked up by input value. The LSC correction table is one.
An unsigned fixed-point format. UQ<m, n> represents a value with m integer bits and n fractional bits.
Message exchange between separate processes. Unsigned IPA modules run in a separate process, so libcamera calls them over IPC.

A stand-in object that takes calls through the same interface instead of calling the IPA module directly, and forwards them to the IPA thread or a separate process. It is generated from the mojom definition at build time.
The file format that defines the functions and types of an IPA interface. The proxy code is generated from it at build time.
The libcamera component that finds a hardware platform's media devices (IPU3, RKISP1 and so on), creates cameras, queues requests to the devices and returns completions. There is one per platform.
The camera ISP in some Intel laptop processors. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
The camera ISP in Rockchip SoCs, the NXP i.MX8MP and others. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
The Arm Mali-C55 camera ISP. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
Straightening an image bent by the lens. The RKISP1 pipeline does it by loading a coordinate table (vertex map) into the DW100 device.
A separate hardware device that corrects distortion by remapping the image according to a coordinate table. It is found in the NXP i.MX8MP and others.
The standard USB webcams follow. libcamera drives these devices with the uvcvideo Pipeline Handler.
The Linux kernel API for cameras and video devices. libcamera controls sensors and ISP devices through it.
The layer that lets an operating system drive different vendors' hardware through one interface. This project ultimately targets an in-house Android Camera HAL.

The standard error numbers Linux functions use to report why they failed. libcamera functions return them as negative values. For example, -ENODEV means no device, -EACCES access denied, -EINVAL an invalid argument, -ENOMEM out of memory and -EXDEV a resource that belongs to another object.
libcamera's debug check macro. In debug builds, a false condition logs a fatal message and aborts execution.
FPS means frames per second.
An environment for running Linux on Windows. This site is built from libcamera compiled and extracted in WSL2.
An external documentation tool whose reading layout and diagram zoom and search rules this site follows. Only the rules were applied; its runner is not used.
Returns an -EEXIST error if there are remaining fences not yet released on the buffer or if a buffer is already registered on the same stream.
ETIMEDOUT is an error code indicating that a call did not complete because the specified time (2000ms based on this file) while waiting for a response during IPC communication was exceeded.
Calling FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() again on a stream that already has buffers allocated returns -EBUSY.
